articles.title: Van Hollen Puts AI at Center of His Challenge to Schumer
articles.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is making the regulation of artificial intelligence a central part of his campaign to lead Senate Democrats , arguing that Congress must move more aggressively to confront the technology's growing risks and that the party needs a leader willing to challenge the powerful companies seeking to shape the rules. articles.title: Why the BAAJA Permitting Reform Bill Is Dividing Climate and Energy Advocates
articles.summary: The Senate voted on Nov. 18 to move forward with the Bipartisan Affordability and American Jobs Act (BAAJA) of 2026, a controversial permitting reform bill that aims to speed up the nation’s ability to build infrastructure and energy —which can often take years under the current process. The bill—which has divided environmentalists and clean energy advocates—will now face a final Senate vote before moving to the House of Representatives. articles.title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth May Be Less a Film than a Vibe
articles.summary: It’s easy to feel nostalgia for the Hollywood filmmaking of the 1970s, when wily young directors succeeded in shaking the big-studio money tree to fund their outlandish, and often brilliant, projects. But we’ve also reached the era where the movies of the 1990s look pretty damn good. Which means David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is probably hitting at the right time. articles.title: What the Midterms Taught Us About the State of America’s Democracy
articles.summary: The recent “Blue Wave” was Democrats’ best election night in years. But Memphis, a majority-Black city whose own congressional seat Democrats had held for more than four decades, will be represented in Congress entirely by Republicans . The day after the midterms, Justin Pearson, the Democratic candidate for Tennessee’s newly drawn Ninth District House seat, may have conceded his race, but he refused to concede to the redistricting.
